prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator, and its first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells.

statement.case_for: I have moved from B018 to B016. After the first round, B018 stands as a single-member position, and the chair's question on whether a method counts as a discovery is one I cannot answer to the standard I would want from a colleague. I still think DMFT is one of the most consequential ideas in theoretical condensed matter, but I put the larger weight on a closed chain from prediction to observation. B016 is the best such chain on the shortlist. Kane and Mele identified the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall state of a time-reversal-invariant insulator, and Molenkamp's group observed helical edge transport in HgTe wells in 2007. It has been reproduced for almost two decades and has changed how band structure, symmetry and spin-orbit coupling are used to classify electronic states. As an electronic-structure theorist, I regard that classification as something calculations now routinely compute, for instance in materials searches. Johansson and Mehlig persuaded me that the 2016 overlap is smaller than I wrote in round 1: the Chern insulator and the Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz physics concern broken time-reversal symmetry, quantized Hall response and defect-driven transitions, whereas Z2 insulators and protected helical edges are a different step. I would draft the citation on the quantum spin Hall effect specifically and say 'observation', not 'verification of quantized transport'.
statement.case_against: The credit is incomplete and I will not claim otherwise. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe as the platform, Zhang is deceased, and the three-dimensional topological insulator work (Fu, Kane and Mele; Moore and Balents; Hasan and others) lies outside the three names. HgTe edge quantization is good in short channels and imperfect in long ones, so the experimental half is weaker than the theory half. Overlap with 2016 is reduced in my mind but not removed, since a reader may treat topological classification as already rewarded. B014 has the cleaner two-name attribution and, by the chair's count, the larger number of explicit supporters. If the committee decides the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang gap cannot be defended, I would accept B014 without strong objection. I also note that I am not moving because B016 has more supporters than B018; the count is not a scientific argument, and I moved because of the discovery-versus-method question and the credit arguments.

responses.point: Danielsson argued in round 1 that B016 is a complete theory-to-experiment chain, that the 2016 prize is neighbouring but distinct, and that the lack of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is a genuine cost but defensible in a citation naming the Z2 prediction and its first observation.
responses.response: In round 1 I said the 2016 overlap could not be dismissed as easily as you did. I now think you were closer to right. Time-reversal-invariant Z2 insulators and Haldane's Chern insulator are different symmetry classes with different edge physics, and the experiment is a separate one. I also accept your reply on DMFT: a method with limited quantitative predictivity does not have the same discovery character as a prediction seen in transport. I still hold that the BHZ omission is a real cost and not just a drafting matter, and the citation should not claim the HgTe proposal. Given that, I can support your configuration.

responses.point: Johansson proposed tying the experimental half of the citation to Molenkamp's observation of edge transport instead of to the proposal, and noted that Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz honoured topological phase transitions and quantized transport, a distinct step from Z2 classification.
responses.response: Your drafting solution is the one I would use, and the distinction you draw on 2016 is what changed my view. I would add that HgTe quantization is imperfect in longer channels, which you raised and Mehlig repeated, so the experimental half is best described as an observation of helical edge transport rather than a precise test of quantization. Your remark that B014 would be cleaner if the HgTe attribution cannot be defended is fair. I do not think the committee can settle that by a count of votes, so I would rather argue the attribution directly now, in the final round.

responses.point: Mehlig, who moved to B016 after reading the ballots, said that the framework is a conceptual change in how band structure and symmetry are understood and that DMFT is a computational method with open points on double counting and on Metzner's role, to be kept for a later year.
responses.response: I agree with most of this. You are right that DMFT is a method whose quantitative use in real materials depends on double-counting and interaction-parameter choices. I do not retreat from the view that the framework is exact in a well-defined limit and systematically improvable, but I accept that the three-name ceiling cannot do justice to the credit between Metzner, Vollhardt, Georges and Kotliar. I would be content to see it considered in a later year. Your point that the Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang gap is not unusual among the candidates is correct, but it is still a real cost here, and I would not want us to treat it as negligible.

responses.point: Kroll holds B014 first, says the lattice clock is a single, well-defined invention with a clean Katori and Ye split, and asked the chair to consider whether his time in Hall's laboratory calls for recusal or only disclosure.
responses.response: I accept that B014 has the cleanest attribution, and I said so in round 1. My remaining difference is about what we are weighing. The 2005 and 2012 prizes make the clock look like a third step in a precision-metrology line, and the pending redefinition of the second is still a prospective application. I would not say that is disqualifying, and for that reason B014 is my first alternative. I welcome your disclosure on Boulder and agree that the chair should settle recusal before any count.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, moved from B021 to B014 on attribution and confirmation grounds, and asked that the citation be written around magic-wavelength trapping and not around optical frequency metrology in general.
responses.response: I understand why attribution moved you, and I share that criterion. On that criterion alone B014 is ahead of B016, because the two names Katori and Ye leave no obvious gap while Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang do. The difference is that I weigh the conceptual change in how electronic phases are classified more heavily than I weigh a clean two-name split. If the committee decides on attribution first, I could vote for B014. Your question about what would move us from one to the other has a short answer for me: a defensible account of the HgTe credit would keep me at B016, and a decision that it cannot be defended would move me to B014.

uncertainties: Whether the HgTe attribution (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, with Zhang deceased) can be defended in a three-name prize, which decides for me between B016 and B014.
Whether the committee reads the 2016 prize as covering Z2 insulators. I now think it does not, but I have not verified chronology details against the nomination files and rely on general knowledge.
How much weight to give imperfect HgTe edge quantization, and whether the experimental half should be described only as an observation of helical edge transport.
Whether I have moved partly because B018 had no other supporters. I have tried to rely on the discovery-versus-method and credit arguments, but I cannot rule out some influence.
statement.conflict_note: I withdraw the B018 field-proximity disclosure as it applies to my preferred ballot, but I keep it on record in case B018 returns as an alternative: DMFT and DFT+DMFT are close to my own research in electronic-structure theory and correlated electrons at Uppsala, and the profile documents no tie to Georges, Kotliar or Vollhardt. For B016, my work on magnetism, spin-orbit effects and electronic structure is in condensed-matter theory near the topological-insulator literature, but my profile records no collaboration with Kane, Mele or Molenkamp, so I disclose the proximity and do not claim a conflict. I have no documented link to Katori or Ye. I note Kroll's and Olsson's disclosures on B014 and leave their handling to the chair.
